claim: Statement 32: 'Estimated total no. of workers in usual status (ps+ss) during Jan - Dec, 2025 (in 000)' = 6,16,368. Rural male 2,66,078; rural female 1,49,914; urban male 1,49,727; urban female 50,649 (in 000)

claim: Statement 7, PLFS 2025, rural+urban persons: own account worker and employer 40.5%, helper in household enterprise 15.6%, all self-employed 56.2%, regular wage/salary 23.6%, casual labour 20.2%. Rural persons 43.2 / 19.3 / 62.4; urban persons 34.0 / 6.4 / 40.4

source_title: MoSPI, Periodic Labour Force Survey Annual Report 2025 (Jan-Dec 2025), Statement 7 (p.17)

claim: DERIVED: self-employed persons = sum over rural/urban x male/female of (SIZE-01 workers x SIZE-02 self-employed share) = 15.27 + 10.60 + 6.05 + 2.05
population: Self-employed workers aged 15+, usual status, all-India
source_title: Derived from SIZE-01 and SIZE-02

claim: DERIVED: own-account workers and employers = 12.32 (rural M) + 5.68 (rural F) + 5.38 (urban M) + 1.45 (urban F); unpaid helpers in household enterprises = 2.95 + 4.93 + 0.67 + 0.60
population: Self-employed workers aged 15+, usual status, all-India
source_title: Derived from SIZE-01 and SIZE-02 (sex x sector shares)
notes: Unpaid helpers are mostly women in family farms and shops (rural female helper share 32.9%). They do not run the business and usually report no earnings, so they are not a borrower.

source_title: MoSPI, Periodic Labour Force Survey Annual Report 2025 (Jan-Dec 2025), Statement 8 (p.19)

claim: Table 20, PLFS 2025: own account worker/employer share within each industry. All-India persons: agriculture 51.3% (helpers 29.6%), secondary 25.0%, trade 55.5%, transport 50.9%, accommodation & food 41.9%, other services 20.9%, tertiary 38.2%

claim: DERIVED: own-account workers and employers IN agriculture = 12.99 crore; OUTSIDE agriculture = 11.84 crore. Method: SIZE-01 workers x Statement 8 industry share x Table 20 own-account share, per sex x sector

claim: DERIVED: non-farm own-account workers and employers in URBAN areas = 6.01 crore (of which trade, transport and services 4.23 crore); in RURAL areas = 5.82 crore
population: Non-farm own-account workers and employers aged 15+, usual status, by PLFS rural/urban
source_title: Derived from SIZE-01, SIZE-05, SIZE-06
notes: PLFS splits only rural vs urban. There is NO city-tier (tier 1/2/3) split in PLFS or anywhere we searched; do not invent one. 'Rural non-farm' includes village shops, transport and artisans.

claim: Table 46: non-agricultural self-employed by location of workplace. Urban persons: no fixed workplace 10.1%, home 26.0%, other than home 64.0%. Rural+urban persons: 7.7% / 35.9% / 56.4%
unit: % of urban non-farm self-employed working from a place other than home
population: Self-employed (incl. helpers) in non-agriculture, usual status, all-India
source_title: MoSPI, Periodic Labour Force Survey Annual Report 2025 (Jan-Dec 2025), Appendix A Table 46
notes: 'Other than home' includes shops, offices, workshops and fixed street spots; it is the nearest PLFS proxy for 'has a shop or premises'. Includes helpers, so do not multiply straight into SIZE-08.

claim: Statement 13: average gross earnings during the last 30 days from self-employment, CWS, 2025: urban person Rs 23,012 (male 26,094, female 10,237); rural person 12,266; all 14,861. 2022 urban: 18,376
population: Self-employed persons in current weekly status, excluding zero/not-reported earnings
source_title: MoSPI, Periodic Labour Force Survey Annual Report 2025 (Jan-Dec 2025), Statement 13 (p.23)
notes: GROSS, single-shot question; PLFS does not say whether business costs are deducted. A MEAN, pulled up by employers; excludes zero earners. Never compare with a gig NET figure.

population: PLFS 2025 annual report
source_title: MoSPI, Periodic Labour Force Survey Annual Report 2025 (Jan-Dec 2025)

claim: 'Only about 10% of the self-employed reported earnings more than Rs 20,000 per month and only about 1% reported earnings more than Rs 50,000 per month'; median self-employed Rs 8,000 (own account Rs 8,000, employers Rs 15,000); self-employed = 70% own account, 26% helpers, 4% employers
unit: % of self-employed reporting > Rs 20,000 a month
population: Self-employed reporting earnings, PLFS 2017-18 unit-level data, all-India
source_title: IDR, 'The stark reality of self-employment', Thampi & Anand (18 Oct 2019)
notes: Article read. Old (2017-18) but the only published distribution we found. Used, with SIZE-14, to scale to 2025.

claim: PLFS 2017-18 average monthly gross earnings of the self-employed: rural Rs 8,430, urban Rs 14,792
population: Self-employed in CWS, PLFS 2017-18, all-India
source_title: MPRA paper 101249 (secondary summary of PLFS 2017-18)
notes: From a search summary of the paper; not checked against the 2017-18 PLFS report itself.

claim: DERIVED: growth in mean self-employment earnings 2017-18 to 2025: urban 23,012 / 14,792 = x1.56; rural 12,266 / 8,430 = x1.46. So Rs 20,000 in 2017-18 is roughly Rs 29,000-31,000 in 2025 money
population: Self-employed in CWS, all-India
source_title: Derived from SIZE-10 and SIZE-13
notes: Assumes the whole distribution scaled by the same factor (shape unchanged). That assumption is untested.

claim: DERIVED (MODEL): share of self-employed earners above Rs 30,000 a month gross in 2025: about 8-11% all-India; about 22-23% urban; about 5-8% rural. Lognormal with mean = SIZE-10 and mean/median ratio 1.25-1.6 (2017-18 implied ~1.25)
population: Self-employed persons reporting earnings, CWS, 2025
source_title: Derived from SIZE-10, SIZE-12, SIZE-14
notes: Cross-check: SIZE-12 scaled by SIZE-14 gives ~10% all-India above ~Rs 30k, matching the model's all-India 8-11%. The URBAN figure is the model's alone; no source publishes it. Least certain number in the funnel.

claim: DERIVED: reachable core = urban non-farm own-account workers and employers earning > Rs 30k gross = 6.01 crore (SIZE-08) x ~23% (SIZE-15) = about 1.4 crore. Range 1.0-1.8 crore if the share is 17-30%
population: Urban, non-farm, own-account workers and employers, > Rs 30k a month gross
source_title: Derived from SIZE-08 and SIZE-15
notes: Second route: ~10% (SIZE-15, all-India) x 24.82 crore own-account+employers (SIZE-04) = ~2.5 crore nationally incl. farmers and rural. Applying an urban-average share to the non-farm subset is an assumption (non-farm earners probably earn a bit more, farmers excluded). The core excludes ~5.8 crore rural non-farm owners, some of whom also clear Rs 30k.

claim: Udyam portal live counter: 'Udyam Registration' 5,42,93,853; 'Udyam Assist Platform (UAP)' 4,33,10,386; total 9,76,04,239 (as of 3 Oct 2026, 10:30 am)
population: Enterprises registered on Udyam (micro, small, medium) and informal micro enterprises on UAP, all-India, cumulative
source_title: Udyam Registration portal homepage counter
notes: Enterprises, not people; one person can register more than one enterprise. UAP entries are informal micro enterprises onboarded by 'assist partners' (banks, NBFCs, SHG channels), often in bulk; they need no GST or PAN. Growth from 8.84 crore (30 Jun 2026, SIZE-18) to 9.76 crore in ~3 months shows bulk onboarding, so registrations overstate active businesses.

claim: 'over 8.84 crore enterprises have registered on the Udyam Registration Portal (URP) and the Udyam Assist Portal (UAP)' as of 30 Jun 2026 (Rajya Sabha written reply); ~9 crore employing 'over 38 crore people' (MSME ministry, 14 Jul 2026)
